ai_scorecard.headline: Western Coast Asphalt: repairs fail far more often than peers
ai_scorecard.summary: Western Coast Asphalt Co did 299 jobs in 24 wards, spending Rs 1.75 cr. Met repair deadline on 47.2% of jobs, against a city average of 49.6%. Repairs failed again on 38.8% of jobs; peers doing the same methods in similar conditions would expect 24.9%. Flooding explains part of this; 118 jobs fell in heavy-rain weeks. Median billing is 6.5% above the rate card. Records flag 5 jobs billed Rs 4.44 lakh above expected, such as WO25-01005 at Rs 2.79 lakh against Rs 90,000. Three repeat bills worth Rs 76,329, such as WO25-02458, appear to duplicate earlier jobs. Another 22 jobs worth Rs 7.76 lakh were paid while roads were under defect liability, e.g. WO25-00326. These need checking; they are not findings of wrongdoing.
doing_well: Median billing is only 6.5% above the rate card.
Dewatering pump jobs reopened 2 of 17 times, the lowest rate of any method.
ai_scorecard.improve: Review cold mix patch jobs, which reopened 38 of 73 times, and check why they fail.

charges.claim: 22 jobs were paid while the road was still under its Defect Liability Period, when the contractor should still be responsible for repairs. BMC paid Rs 7.76 lakh (Rs 775,984) across these 22 jobs. Four examples are listed here. Check whether each payment was allowed under the contract terms.

5 jobs were billed above the expected cost. The excess over expected is Rs 4.44 lakh (Rs 443,627). Bills ran between 1.56x and 3.10x the expected amount. Check these bills against the rate sheet and the measured area. Rain or flooding does not explain a bill that is higher than the expected cost.

3 jobs have no linked complaint. Each one repeats an earlier job by the same contractor on the same road, 1 to 2 days before. The total is Rs 76,329. Check whether these were real separate jobs or duplicate entries.

38.8% of this contractor's repairs were reopened. Peers doing the same methods in similarly flood-prone wards in similar rain expect 24.9%. That is 1.56x the peer rate. The city average is 24.5%. Flooding explains part of the gap, since high-flood wards reopen at 42.9% against 34.5% in low-lying wards. The gap to expected still remains. SLA was met on 47.2% of jobs, against a city average of 49.6%. The amount shown is total spend across 299 jobs, not a loss estimate.

mitigations.point: Flooding explains part of the repeat-failure gap. Repairs in high-flood wards reopen more often than repairs in low-lying wards, so location matters.
mitigations.based_on: reopen_by_flood_band: high-flood band 42.9% reopened (98 jobs) vs low-lying band 34.5% (55 jobs); mid band 37.7% (146 jobs)

mitigations.point: Heavy rain touched many of the jobs. Rain soon after a repair may have caused some of the reopened work, which is outside the contractor's control.
mitigations.based_on: jobs_in_heavy_rain_weeks: 118 of 299 jobs

mitigations.point: Most rates look close to typical, and overbilling affects a small share of jobs. The contractor's rates are not far above the median, and the overbilled jobs are a small part of the total.
mitigations.based_on: median_rate_ratio 1.065; overbilled_jobs 5 of 299 jobs (overbilled_pct_of_jobs 1.7)

mitigations.point: The data does not excuse everything. Rain does not explain payments made during the Defect Liability Period, such as WO25-00326 (Rs 198,148 on RD0155), or bills above expected cost, such as WO25-01005 (billed Rs 279,310 vs expected Rs 90,000). After allowing for flood wards, repeat failures still run above peers (38.8% vs 24.9% expected), so this gap needs checking. Heavy rain could explain some quick repeat visits such as WO25-02458, WO25-02477 and WO25-02457, but the records do not show that, so they should be checked against the job records.
mitigations.based_on: dlp_paid_examples (WO25-00326); overbilled_examples (WO25-01005, evidence ratio 3.10x); ghost_bill_examples (WO25-02458, WO25-02477, WO25-02457); reopen_pct 38.8 vs expected_reopen_pct 24.9; reopen_vs_peers 1.56

upheld: 22 jobs were paid during the Defect Liability Period, totalling Rs 7.76 L. Examples WO25-00326, WO25-00913, WO25-00824 and WO25-02025 sit on roads resurfaced within that period, so each payment needs a contract check.
5 jobs were billed above expected cost, with Rs 4.44 L excess. WO25-01005 was billed Rs 2.79 L against an expected Rs 0.90 L (3.10x). Rain does not explain this gap.

3 repeat entries have no linked complaint and total Rs 76,329 (WO25-02458, WO25-02477, WO25-02457). Each repeats an earlier job on the same road 1 to 2 days before. Check whether they are real separate jobs or duplicates.
Repeat failures run at 38.8% against 24.9% expected from peers, or 1.56x. This gap remains after allowing for flood-prone wards and heavy-rain weeks.
accepted_context: High-flood wards reopen more often: 42.9% against 34.5% in low-lying wards.
Heavy rain touched 118 of 299 jobs, and peer expectations already allow for flood and rain.
Most rates are close to typical, with a median rate ratio of 1.065.
Overbilling affects 5 of 299 jobs (1.7%). This is a small share, but it does not clear the five jobs listed.
judge.ruling: Three of the four charges stand and need checking before further payment. The payments made during the Defect Liability Period show these roads were still under contractor responsibility, so the contract basis must be confirmed. The five overbilled jobs sit well above expected cost, and rain does not explain that. The three repeat entries may be real separate jobs, but the records do not show it. The repeat-failure rate stays above peers even after flood and rain are allowed for. This is a check, not a finding of fraud. Typical rates and the small share of overbilled jobs are fair points in the contractor's favour.
judge.action: Check the 22 Defect Liability Period payments (Rs 7.76 L) and the 5 overbilled jobs (Rs 4.44 L excess) against the contract terms and rate sheet, and recover only the amounts the records cannot justify.

ai_scorecard.headline: Mahalaxmi Civil: repairs fail more than peers, many bills exceed rate card
ai_scorecard.summary: Mahalaxmi Civil Contractors did 303 jobs in 24 wards, spending Rs 1.62 cr. Only 39.3% of jobs met the time target, against a city average of 49.6%. Repairs reopened 37.6% of the time, 1.55 times the rate peers achieve in similar conditions (24.3% expected). Median billing is 1.079 times the rate card. 44 jobs were billed above the rate card, an excess of Rs 17.15 lakh. Ten bills worth Rs 5.64 lakh repeat an earlier job with no linked complaint. 33 jobs worth Rs 8.45 lakh were paid while still under the Defect Liability Period. The records do not show how long repairs lasted. Heavy rain and low-lying wards may explain part of the reopen rate. These are patterns to verify, not findings of wrongdoing.
doing_well: Median billing is close to the rate card, at 1.079 times.
Excavation, pipeline and PQC repairs reopened only 1 of 10 jobs.
ai_scorecard.improve: Check the 44 above-rate-card bills, starting with WO25-01576, and verify the 10 repeat bills before further payment.

charges.claim: 44 jobs were billed above the rate card, with Rs 17.15 L more billed than expected in total. Examples bill two to three times the expected cost for the same type of repair. Each bill should be checked against the rate card and the measurement records.

10 bills worth Rs 5.64 L appear to repeat earlier jobs on the same road segment, and no complaint is linked to them. Each repeat sits 1 to 4 days after the earlier job. Some repeats may reflect real new damage, especially after heavy rain. Officials should confirm that each visit happened and was needed.

33 jobs were paid Rs 8.45 L while the road was still under its Defect Liability Period. This means the contractor was still responsible for these repairs. Heavy rain can cause new damage, so the cause should be checked before deciding who pays.

mitigations.point: Rain is part of the picture, but the peer benchmark already allows for rainy weeks. Peers in equally rainy weeks reopen 24.3% of jobs, against 37.6% here. Heavy rain fell during 119 of the 303 jobs, and new rain damage can reopen a fresh repair.
mitigations.based_on: scorecard: reopen_pct 37.6, expected_reopen_pct 24.3, reopen_vs_peers 1.55, jobs 303; jobs_in_heavy_rain_weeks 119

mitigations.point: Flood-prone wards may explain some reopenings. High-band wards reopen 40.4% of jobs, mid-band 38.2%, and low-band 31.7%. Even low-band wards are above the city average of 24.5%, so flooding does not explain the whole gap.
mitigations.based_on: reopen_by_flood_band: high 104 jobs 40.4%, mid 136 jobs 38.2%, low 63 jobs 31.7%; city_average reopen_pct 24.5

mitigations.point: Most jobs are priced close to the rate card. The median rate ratio is 1.079, and 44 jobs (14.5%) are flagged. Rain is unlikely to explain bills of two to three times the expected cost, such as WO25-01576 at 3.10x. These bills still need a check against the rate card and measurement records. Rs 17.15 L is the excess in total.
mitigations.based_on: median_rate_ratio 1.079; overbilled_jobs 44; overbilled_pct_of_jobs 14.5; overbilled_excess_inr 1715259; WO25-01576 ratio 3.10x

mitigations.point: Rain does not clearly explain the repeat bills. WO25-02462, WO25-02499, WO25-02473 and WO25-02481 each have no linked complaint. Each sits 1.0 to 4.0 days after an earlier job on the same road. Officials should confirm each visit happened and was needed. Rs 5.64 L is at stake across these 10 bills.
mitigations.based_on: ghost_bill_examples: WO25-02462 repeats WO25-01977 3.0 days earlier; WO25-02499 repeats WO25-01444 1.0 days earlier; WO25-02473 repeats WO25-00328 4.0 days earlier; WO25-02481 repeats WO25-00367 2.0 days earlier; ghost_bills 10, ghost_bills_inr 564028

upheld: 44 jobs billed above the rate card, Rs 17.15L excess; examples WO25-01576 (3.10x), WO25-01011 (2.24x), WO25-01151 (2.62x), WO25-01184 (2.23x), WO25-00700 (2.67x) and WO25-01782 (1.99x) are not explained by rain
Reopen rate of 37.6% against 24.3% expected for peers (1.55x) remains after the rain and flood allowance

10 repeat-visit bills worth Rs 5.64L have no linked complaint and sit 1.0 to 4.0 days after an earlier job on the same road (e.g. WO25-02462, WO25-02499, WO25-02473, WO25-02481); visits need confirmation
33 jobs worth Rs 8.45L were paid while the road was under its Defect Liability Period (e.g. WO25-01529, WO25-01947, WO25-00206, WO25-02258); the cause still needs checking before deciding who pays
accepted_context: Heavy rain fell during 119 of 303 jobs, and rain can cause new damage that reopens a fresh repair
Low-lying wards reopen more often (high band 40.4%, mid 38.2%, low 31.7%), which explains part of the gap
Median rate ratio is 1.079, so most jobs are priced close to the rate card; the overbilling is concentrated in 44 jobs (14.5%)
Some repeat visits may reflect real new damage after heavy rain, so they are not proof of a bad bill
Rain may explain some Defect Liability Period repairs, but the records do not show this for each job
judge.ruling: Mahalaxmi Civil Contractors (CT03) shows a serious performance concern. Repairs reopen 37.6% of the time, against 24.3% expected for peers in similar rain and flooding. Rain and low-lying wards explain part of this, but not all of it. The clearest issue is billing: 44 jobs were billed above the rate card, with Rs 17.15L excess. Examples such as WO25-01576 were billed 3.10 times the expected cost. Ten repeat-visit bills (Rs 5.64L) and 33 jobs paid during the Defect Liability Period (Rs 8.45L) need checks before any conclusion is drawn.
judge.action: Verify the 44 overbilled jobs, starting with WO25-01576, WO25-01011 and WO25-00700, against the rate card and measurement records, and recover any excess confirmed, up to Rs 17.15L.

ai_scorecard.headline: CT07 Arabian Sea Engineering: repairs reopen more often than peers
ai_scorecard.summary: Arabian Sea Engineering (CT07) did 328 jobs across 24 wards, spending Rs 1.86 cr. Only 43.6% of jobs met the time target, below the city average of 49.6%. Repairs reopened 32.3% of the time, against 24.7% expected for the same methods, flood-prone wards and rainy weeks. Rain and low-lying roads explain part of this, but mid-band wards reopened most often. The median bill is 1.08 times the rate card. 38 jobs were billed above the rate card, about Rs 19.7 L in excess. Three bills appear to repeat earlier jobs on the same road with no linked complaint, and should be checked. BMC paid Rs 12.55 L on 42 jobs still under the Defect Liability Period. The records do not show how long repairs lasted.
doing_well: Median bill is 1.08 times the rate card, a small gap
Work spread across 24 wards and 328 jobs
ai_scorecard.improve: Check the 38 jobs billed above the rate card, starting with the largest gaps such as WO25-01626 and WO25-00197, against their rate card lines.

charges.claim: 38 jobs were billed above the rate card, with a total excess of Rs 19.7 L (Rs 19,67,499). That is 11.6% of the contractor's 328 jobs. The largest examples are listed here. Rain or low-lying ground does not explain bills above the rate card, so each example should be checked against the rate card and the measurement records.

BMC paid Rs 12.6 L (Rs 12,55,419) for 42 jobs on roads still inside the Defect Liability Period. Under that period, the contractor should normally repair defects at its own cost. Each example below is on a road resurfaced in 2023 or 2024. The records should be checked to confirm whether these payments were correct or whether the defect rules applied.

Three bills totalling Rs 1.85 L (Rs 1,85,356) have no complaint linked to them. Each one repeats a job the same contractor did on the same road 2 to 3 days earlier. The records should be checked to confirm that each job was needed and was actually carried out.

mitigations.point: Heavy rain explains part of the repair failures. 144 of the 328 jobs (about 44%) fell in heavy-rain weeks. The expected reopen rate of 24.7% already allows for flood-prone wards and rainy weeks, but the contractor's 32.3% is still 7.6 points higher. That remaining gap is not excused by rain.
mitigations.based_on: jobs_in_heavy_rain_weeks 144 of 328 jobs; reopen_pct 32.3 vs expected_reopen_pct 24.7; peer_note says expected rate covers flood-prone wards and rainy weeks

mitigations.point: Low-lying ground does not clearly explain the pattern. Jobs in high-lying-risk wards reopened at 30.4%, which is below the contractor's overall 32.3%. Mid-band wards reopened at 35.2%, the highest of the three groups. Flooding may still affect individual jobs, but it does not account for the overall gap.
mitigations.based_on: reopen_by_flood_band: high 30.4% (112 jobs), low 27.8% (54 jobs), mid 35.2% (162 jobs)

mitigations.point: Some flagged payments are below the expected cost, and the at-risk figure counts the full payment rather than the gap. For WO25-02380, Rs 153,230 was paid against an expected Rs 180,000. For WO25-02482 and WO25-02479, the costs were Rs 87,046 and Rs 80,886 against expected Rs 93,600 and Rs 90,000. Each of these three bills also repeats an earlier job on the same road 2 to 3 days before. Rain may have forced genuine re-work, so the records should show whether each job was needed.
mitigations.based_on: dlp_paid_examples WO25-02380 cost_inr 153230 vs expected_inr 180000; ghost_bill_examples WO25-02482, WO25-02479 cost and expected values; evidence notes repeat jobs 2.0 and 3.0 days earlier

mitigations.point: Rain does not explain the overbilling, and the contractor's on-time record is weak. 38 jobs (11.6%) were billed above the rate card, and the largest example, WO25-01626, cost Rs 331,958 against an expected Rs 110,000. Only 43.6% of jobs met the deadline, against a city average of 49.6%. The median rate ratio of 1.08 also needs explaining.
mitigations.based_on: overbilled_pct_of_jobs 11.6; overbilled_examples WO25-01626 cost_inr 331958 vs expected_inr 110000; sla_met_pct 43.6 vs city_average sla_met_pct 49.6; median_rate_ratio 1.08

upheld: 38 jobs (11.6%) billed above the rate card, excess Rs 19.7 L. Largest: WO25-01626 at Rs 331,958 vs expected Rs 110,000 (3.02x).
Reopen rate 32.3% vs expected 24.7%, which is 1.31 times peers. Rain and flood bands do not explain this gap.
42 jobs paid Rs 12.6 L on roads still under Defect Liability Period, e.g. WO25-02068 and WO25-00985. Records must confirm whether the payments were correct.
Three repeat bills with no linked complaint, Rs 1.85 L: WO25-02482, WO25-02479, WO25-02471. Records must show each job was needed and done.
On-time rate 43.6% vs city average 49.6%.

judge.ruling: Serious concern. Rain does not explain the overbilling. The rate card was exceeded on 38 jobs, Rs 19.7 L in total. The Defence Liability Period payments (Rs 12.6 L) and three repeat bills (Rs 1.85 L) need record checks before any finding. Some at-risk figures overstate the gap and should be corrected.
judge.action: Check the 38 overbilled jobs against the rate card and measurement records, starting with WO25-01626, WO25-00197 and WO25-01358, and recover any excess confirmed.

ai_scorecard.headline: Shivneri Construction: mostly within peer norms, with billing checks needed
ai_scorecard.summary: Shivneri Construction did 289 jobs across 24 wards, worth Rs 1.47 cr. Repairs were reopened 26.3% of the time, against 24.0% expected for similar work and 24.5% city-wide. Five jobs were billed Rs 1.05 L above expected. Eight bills worth Rs 4.44 L have no linked complaint and repeat earlier jobs on the same road. These should be checked. 29 jobs (Rs 9.62 L) were paid while still under the defect liability period, and this should be reviewed.
doing_well: Repair durability is close to peer expectations (1.1 times peers, against 1.0 as the norm).
Only 5 of 289 jobs (1.7%) were billed above expected cost.
ai_scorecard.improve: Check the eight bills with no linked complaint that repeat earlier jobs, starting with WO25-02494 and WO25-02485, and confirm the 29 defect-period payments before further payments are released.

The largest gap is WO25-00743 on Kalbadevi Road, billed Rs 73,924 against an expected Rs 35,280 (8.4 sqm at Rs 4,200 per sqm). Check the measured area and rate for each job. Each one repeats an earlier job on the same road ID, by the same contractor, 1 to 4 days earlier. For example, WO25-02494 repeats WO25-01235 on RD0115 one day earlier. Check whether a second visit was needed. Heavy rain can cause repeat repairs, and the records show 115 jobs in heavy-rain weeks, so check the rain dates too.

29 jobs, worth Rs 9.62 L (Rs 962,369), were paid while the road was still under its Defect Liability Period. The four examples are on roads resurfaced in 2023 and 2024. WO25-01306 (Rs 178,997) and WO25-00306 (Rs 118,452) are among them. WO25-00743 also appears in the overbilling concern. Check whether the payment rules allowed these payments, and whether the contractor was asked to fix these roads first.

The records still show no linked citizen complaint for any of the eight bills, which total Rs 4.44 L, so this part is not excused by the data.

The verdict reflects items that still need checking, not proven fault.
judge.action: Ask the ward office to check the DLP payment rules and the measured area and rate for WO25-00743 first, then review the other flagged jobs before any further payment to this contractor.

mitigations.based_on: dlp_paid_examples: cost_inr and expected_inr for WO25-02034, WO25-02366, WO25-01638, WO25-01994; scorecard dlp_paid_jobs 32, dlp_paid_inr 1304588

upheld: Four repeat jobs worth Rs 3.17 L have no linked complaint: WO25-02465, WO25-02488, WO25-02464 and WO25-02459. Each repeats an earlier job on the same road 1 to 3 days before.
Five jobs were billed Rs 2.32 L above expected. WO25-01502 on CST Road is the clearest case at 2.53x (Rs 2,16,234 vs Rs 85,500).
32 jobs (Rs 13.05 L) were paid while their roads were still under the Defect Liability Period. WO25-01994 was paid Rs 1,48,557 vs Rs 1,16,100 expected.
accepted_context: Reopen rate of 26.7% is close to the 24.6% expected for similar wards and weather, and near the city average of 24.5%.
139 of 337 jobs were done in heavy rain weeks, which may explain some repeat failures.

Three of the four defect-period examples (WO25-02034, WO25-02366, WO25-01638) were paid below expected.
judge.ruling: Konkan Roadcon Pvt Ltd (CT02) has a mixed record. Four repeat jobs worth Rs 3.17 L lack linked complaints and need checking. Five jobs worth Rs 2.32 L were billed above expected. WO25-01502 at 2.53x is the clearest case, and its measured area and rate must be confirmed. The 32 jobs paid under the Defect Liability Period (Rs 13.05 L) need a check of whether the defect obligation applied. Rain and measurement differences explain some gaps, but not WO25-01502. Reopen rates are near peers. These are records to verify, not proof of wrongdoing.
judge.action: Withhold further payment on WO25-01502 and the four repeat jobs until complaint records and measured area and rate are verified.

ai_scorecard.headline: Sahyadri Infra Works: good durability and speed; billing items to check
ai_scorecard.summary: Sahyadri Infra Works did 337 jobs across 24 wards, worth Rs 1.72 cr. It met its response target on 62.3% of jobs, against a city average of 49.6%. Repairs reopened 13.6% of the time. Peers doing similar work in similar conditions see 24.7%. Typical job cost is 6.2% above the rate card median. Three jobs were billed above expected cost, Rs 4.43 L over expected in total, including WO25-00611 at 2.28 times expected. Eight bills worth Rs 4.93 L have no linked complaint and repeat a recent job on the same road. These should be checked. Forty-one jobs worth Rs 15.31 L were paid while still under the Defect Liability Period. Low-lying wards reopen more often, and heavy rain may explain part of this.
doing_well: Repairs hold up better than peers: 13.6% reopened against 24.7% expected.
Meets response targets more often than the city average: 62.3% against 49.6%.
ai_scorecard.improve: Check the eight repeat-looking bills and the three overbilled jobs, and record whether the excess cost was justified.

charges.claim: Three jobs were billed well above expected cost. Together they are Rs 4.43 L above expected. WO25-00611 billed Rs 410,330 against Rs 180,000 expected (2.28x). WO25-01723 billed Rs 315,328 against Rs 180,000 (1.75x). WO25-01003 billed Rs 147,422 against Rs 70,000 (2.11x). The records give no flood-related reason for these gaps. Check the bills against measurement sheets and site records.

Eight jobs totalling Rs 4.93 L are flagged as possible ghost bills. Each has no linked complaint. Each repeats an earlier job by the same contractor on the same road, 1 to 4 days before. Examples: WO25-02486 repeats WO25-01255 three days earlier. WO25-02480 repeats WO25-00143 two days earlier. WO25-02500 repeats WO25-01837 one day earlier. WO25-02470 repeats WO25-01327 four days earlier. Check whether each job was done on site, and whether it was done only once.

41 jobs worth Rs 15.31 L were paid while the road was still under the Defect Liability Period. These roads were resurfaced recently and should still be covered by the contractor. Examples: WO25-00491 (Rs 2.31 L, RD0078 resurfaced 2025-03-17), WO25-00677 (Rs 1.64 L, RD0220 resurfaced 2024-02-17), WO25-00691 (Rs 1.00 L, RD0200 resurfaced 2023-05-21), and WO25-01723 (Rs 3.15 L, RD0271 resurfaced 2023-02-28). Fair note: overall reopen rate is 13.6% against 24.7% expected, so most repairs are holding up better than peers. The question is whether these payments were due under the DLP terms. Check the DLP terms for each road.

mitigations.point: Repairs are holding up better than peers. The reopen rate is 13.6% against 24.7% expected, a ratio of 0.55, and below the city average of 24.5%.
mitigations.based_on: scorecard: reopen_pct 13.6, expected_reopen_pct 24.7, reopen_vs_peers 0.55; city_average reopen_pct 24.5

mitigations.point: Typical pricing is close to peers. The median rate ratio is 1.062. Only 3 of 337 jobs (0.9%) were billed above expected, so the overbilling looks confined to a few jobs.
mitigations.based_on: scorecard: median_rate_ratio 1.062, overbilled_jobs 3, jobs 337, overbilled_pct_of_jobs 0.9

mitigations.point: Heavy rain is a fair context for delivery. 147 of 337 jobs fell in heavy rain weeks, yet SLA was met on 62.3% of jobs, above the city figure of 49.6%. Rain does not explain the billing gaps on WO25-00611, WO25-01723 or WO25-01003, because the records give no flood-related reason for them.
mitigations.based_on: scorecard: jobs_in_heavy_rain_weeks 147, sla_met_pct 62.3; city_average sla_met_pct 49.6; auditor charge on WO25-00611, WO25-01723, WO25-01003

mitigations.point: The data does not excuse the rest. The 8 ghost-bill jobs (Rs 4.93 L) and the 41 DLP payments (Rs 15.31 L) have no flood-related explanation in the records. Low-lying wards may explain some slow work, but the 21.2% reopen rate in the low-lying band does not explain billing or payment gaps. Repeats 1 to 4 days after an earlier job could be real rain-related redo work, but no complaint is linked, so each must be checked on site and against DLP terms.
mitigations.based_on: ghost_bill_examples WO25-02486, WO25-02480, WO25-02500, WO25-02470; dlp_paid_examples WO25-01723, WO25-00491, WO25-00677, WO25-00691; reopen_by_flood_band low 21.2 (66 jobs); scorecard ghost_bills 8, dlp_paid_jobs 41

upheld: WO25-00611, WO25-01723 and WO25-01003 were billed Rs 4.43L above expected (2.28x, 1.75x, 2.11x), and the records give no flood-related reason for the gaps.

8 jobs worth Rs 4.93L are flagged as possible ghost bills, including WO25-02486, WO25-02480, WO25-02500 and WO25-02470. None has a linked complaint, and each repeats an earlier same-contractor job 1 to 4 days before. Site checks are needed.

41 jobs worth Rs 15.31L were paid while their roads were still under the Defect Liability Period, including WO25-00491, WO25-00677, WO25-00691 and WO25-01723. The DLP terms for each road need checking.
accepted_context: Reopen rate is 13.6% against 24.7% expected (ratio 0.55), and below the city average of 24.5%.
Median rate ratio is 1.062, and only 3 of 337 jobs (0.9%) were billed above expected.
SLA was met on 62.3% of jobs against a city figure of 49.6%, across 147 jobs in heavy rain weeks.
Low-lying wards may explain some slow work. The low-band reopen rate is 21.2% (66 jobs).
Repeats 1 to 4 days apart could be real rain-related redo work, but this is unproven until checked on site.
judge.ruling: Sahyadri Infra Works (CT01) performs well overall. Its reopen rate and SLA results are better than peers and the city. Overbilling is confined to three jobs, not a wider pattern. However, the records do not explain three billing gaps (Rs 4.43L), eight repeat jobs (Rs 4.93L) or 41 payments made under the Defect Liability Period (Rs 15.31L). Rain does not explain the billing or payment gaps. These are open questions, not findings of wrongdoing. They need checking against measurement sheets, site records and DLP terms.
judge.action: Before any further payment, check the three overbilled jobs against measurement sheets, check the 41 DLP-paid jobs against each road's DLP terms, and confirm on site that the eight repeat jobs were actually done.

why: Within peer norms on durability, billing and speed.

ai_scorecard.headline: Mithi Infra: fewer reopened repairs than peers, but billing needs checks
ai_scorecard.summary: Mithi Infra Projects did 319 jobs across 24 wards, with spend of Rs 1.71 cr. It met its repair deadline on 51.7% of jobs, slightly above the city average of 49.6%. Repairs reopened 11.6% of the time, against an expected 24.0% for similar work in similar conditions. The median price was 1.043 times the rate card, about 4% above it. Records show 10 jobs billed Rs 8.02 L above expected cost. They also show 4 repeat bills worth Rs 2.91 L with no linked complaint. A further 47 jobs worth Rs 13.92 L were paid while still under the Defect Liability Period. These are records to check, not findings of wrongdoing. Heavy rain weeks account for 125 of the jobs. The records here do not give repair durations.
doing_well: Reopen rate of 11.6% is about half the 24.0% expected for similar work.
Median price is 1.043 times the rate card, close to standard.
ai_scorecard.improve: Check the 10 overbilled jobs and the 4 repeat bills against the rate card and site records before further payment.

charges.claim: 10 jobs were billed Rs 8.02 L above expected cost (Rs 802,064 excess, 3.1% of jobs). The six largest examples are listed here. Five are desilting jobs billed 2.1 to 2.9 times the expected rate. Check the measured quantities and bill breakdowns before drawing conclusions. Heavy rain may increase desilting work, but it does not explain a bill this far above the expected cost.

Four jobs look like repeats of earlier jobs by the same contractor. Each was billed 2 to 4 days after a similar job on the same road segment, and no complaint is linked to any of them. Together they came to Rs 2.91 L. Check whether the work was actually done twice, and whether the earlier jobs were paid in full.

BMC paid Rs 13.92 L for 47 jobs on roads still under the Defect Liability Period. Four examples are listed here, each worth Rs 1.31 L to Rs 1.77 L. The records do not show whether these payments were for defect repairs or for planned work. Check the payment terms and whether the contractor's warranty covered these repairs.

mitigations.point: Repairs by this contractor fail less often than peers. Only 11.6% were reopened, against an expected 24.0%.
mitigations.based_on: scorecard: reopen_pct 11.6, expected_reopen_pct 24.0, reopen_vs_peers 0.48

mitigations.point: Most jobs are priced close to expected cost. The median rate is 1.043 times expected. The overbilling sits in a small group: 10 of 319 jobs (3.1%), with Rs 8.02 L above expected. The share is small, but the amount is not excused.
mitigations.based_on: scorecard: median_rate_ratio 1.043, overbilled_jobs 10, overbilled_pct_of_jobs 3.1, overbilled_excess_inr 802064

mitigations.point: Rain and low-lying ground may explain part of the workload. 125 of 319 jobs fell in heavy-rain weeks. Jobs in high-lying wards reopened less often (9.7%) than low-lying (12.9%) or mid-band (13.0%) jobs. Rain may explain more desilting work, but it does not explain desilting bills at 2.1 to 2.9 times expected, such as WO25-02266 and WO25-01496.
mitigations.based_on: jobs_in_heavy_rain_weeks 125; reopen_by_flood_band; overbilled_examples WO25-02266, WO25-01496

mitigations.point: The data does not excuse the four repeat-looking jobs. Each was billed 2 to 4 days after a similar job on the same segment, and no complaint is linked. No rain reason is recorded for these repeats. Check whether the work was done twice, and whether the earlier jobs were paid in full. The Rs 13.92 L paid for 47 jobs under the Defect Liability Period also needs checking against warranty terms.
mitigations.based_on: ghost_bill_examples WO25-02467, WO25-02492, WO25-02476, WO25-02466; ghost_bills 4, ghost_bills_inr 291429; dlp_paid_jobs 47, dlp_paid_inr 1391883

upheld: Overbilling: 10 jobs billed Rs 8.02 L above expected cost. Six examples were billed 2.1 to 2.9 times expected: WO25-02266 (2.89x), WO25-01496 (2.62x), WO25-02275 (2.88x), WO25-02098 (2.86x), WO25-00287 (2.23x), WO25-00019 (2.14x). Rain does not explain these ratios.

Repeat-looking jobs: four jobs worth Rs 2.91 L (WO25-02467, WO25-02492, WO25-02476, WO25-02466) were each billed 2 to 4 days after a similar job on the same segment, with no linked complaint. Whether the work was done twice is not yet verified.

Defect Liability Period payments: Rs 13.92 L was paid for 47 jobs on roads still under warranty. Examples WO25-01369, WO25-00106, WO25-01158 and WO25-01517 need checking against warranty terms and payment type.
accepted_context: Reopen rate is 11.6% against an expected 24.0%, so repairs fail less often than peers (0.48 of expected).
Median rate is 1.043 times expected, so most jobs are priced close to cost.
Heavy rain may explain part of the workload: 125 of 319 jobs fell in heavy-rain weeks, and rain may explain some extra desilting work.
WO25-01369, WO25-00106 and WO25-01158 were billed below expected cost, so the question there is warranty coverage, not rate.
WO25-02467 was billed below expected cost (Rs 105,458 vs Rs 110,000), so the question there is duplication, not rate.
SLA met on 51.7% of jobs, slightly above the city average of 49.6%.
judge.ruling: Mithi Infra Projects (CT08) performs well on durability and median pricing. The records show a concentrated problem: six example jobs were billed 2.1 to 2.9 times expected cost, and rain does not explain that. Four repeat-looking jobs (Rs 2.91 L) and Rs 13.92 L paid under the Defect Liability Period also need checking. These are questions the records raise, not findings of wrongdoing. The verdict is Needs improvement because the concern sits in a small set of jobs.
judge.action: Pause further payment on the six listed overbilled jobs, verify their measured quantities and bill breakdowns, and recover any confirmed excess, starting with WO25-02266 (Rs 1.70 L at risk).

why: Within peer norms on durability, billing and speed.

ai_scorecard.headline: Deccan Paving: faster repairs and fewer reopenings, but billing needs checks
ai_scorecard.summary: Deccan Paving Solutions (CT05) completed 287 jobs across 24 wards, costing about Rs 1.41 cr. Its SLA was met on 59.6% of jobs, against a city average of 49.6%. Repairs reopened 9.1% of the time, against 24.4% expected for similar work and a city average of 24.5%. Median rates sit close to the rate card (1.015 times). Four jobs were billed Rs 3.58 L above expected cost, about 1.4% of jobs. Five bills worth Rs 2.20 L have no linked complaint; the examples repeat a recent job on the same road. Rs 6.63 L was paid for 28 jobs still under their Defect Liability Period. Heavy rain and low-lying wards may explain some delays and failures. These bills are flagged for checking, not proven wrong.
doing_well: Repairs last longer: 9.1% reopened, against 24.4% expected for similar work.
SLA met on 59.6% of jobs, above the city average of 49.6%.
ai_scorecard.improve: Check the flagged bills first, starting with WO25-01942 (billed Rs 2,40,402 against Rs 90,000 expected) and WO25-02487, which repeats WO25-01156 three days earlier. Also confirm why Rs 6.63 L was paid on jobs still under the Defect Liability Period, such as WO25-00523.

charges.claim: Four jobs were billed above expected cost, adding up to Rs 3.58 L above expected (1.4% of jobs). The largest is WO25-01942 on Clare Road: billed Rs 2,40,402 against Rs 90,000 expected (2.67x). WO25-00140 on Marve Road was 2.40x expected, WO25-00382 on Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Road was 2.29x, and WO25-01812 on Juhu Tara Road was 1.71x. Check measured quantities, line-item bills and site photos for these four jobs. The expected figure is a per-job benchmark, so extra work or pumping needed in flood-prone wards may explain part of the gap.

Five bills totaling Rs 2.20 L have no linked complaint. The four examples named in the records each repeat an earlier job by the same contractor on the same road segment, 1 to 4 days before. WO25-02487 (Rs 76,647) repeats WO25-01156 3 days earlier. WO25-02461 (Rs 64,531) repeats WO25-01323 4 days earlier. WO25-02475 (Rs 45,505) repeats WO25-00167 1 day earlier. WO25-02456 (Rs 18,824) repeats WO25-00606 4 days earlier. Check whether the repeat work was needed, and look for crew logs, photos and inspection records. The fifth job is not named in the records.

28 jobs, totaling Rs 6.63 L, were paid while the road was still under the Defect Liability Period, which means it had been resurfaced recently. Examples: WO25-00523 on Kurla Andheri Road (Rs 1,68,417; RD0220 resurfaced 2024-02-17), WO25-02424 on Veer Nariman Road (Rs 85,277; RD0007 resurfaced 2024-02-22), WO25-01164 on Western Express Highway (Rs 51,451; RD0107 resurfaced 2025-05-01), and WO25-00274 on Sion Trombay Road (Rs 42,608; RD0236 resurfaced 2024-02-03). Check whether each job was a defect the contractor should have fixed at no charge, and whether the DLP terms were applied. Heavy rain may explain some new damage, since 120 of the contractor's jobs fell in heavy-rain weeks, so each case needs a site check. The overall scorecard is Good, with a reopen rate of 9.1% against 24.4% expected.

mitigations.point: The reopen rate is low overall. 9.1% of jobs reopened against an expected 24.4% for peers, and the city average is 24.5%. This suggests durable repairs across the contract, but it does not explain the four overbilled jobs or the 28 DLP-paid jobs.
mitigations.based_on: scorecard: reopen_pct 9.1, expected_reopen_pct 24.4, reopen_vs_peers 0.37; city_average reopen_pct 24.5

mitigations.point: Heavy rain may explain some new damage. 120 of the 287 jobs fell in heavy-rain weeks, and rain may have caused new defects on recently resurfaced roads such as WO25-01164 on Western Express Highway. Flooding does not clearly explain reopens, though: the high low-lying band reopened at 4.8% and the low band at 13.7%. Each DLP case still needs a site check to decide whether the contractor should have fixed it at no charge.
mitigations.based_on: jobs_in_heavy_rain_weeks 120; reopen_by_flood_band: high 4.8%, low 13.7%, mid 10.7%; WO25-01164 RD0107 resurfaced 2025-05-01

mitigations.point: Some overbilled jobs involve pumping or heavy desilting, which may need more labour and time in flood-prone wards. These include WO25-00382 (dewatering pump) and WO25-01942 and WO25-00140 (drain or desilting). The Rs 60,000, Rs 90,000 and Rs 70,000 expected figures are per-job benchmarks, so site conditions may explain part of the gap. The records do not yet prove this, so measured quantities and line-item bills must be checked. Overall billing is close to peers, with a median rate ratio of 1.015 and only 1.4% of jobs flagged.
mitigations.based_on: overbilled_examples WO25-00382, WO25-01942, WO25-00140 with expected_inr per job; scorecard median_rate_ratio 1.015, overbilled_pct_of_jobs 1.4

mitigations.point: Some repeat jobs with no linked complaint cost less than the benchmark. A repeat may reflect fresh damage after rain rather than a false bill. WO25-02475 (Rs 45,505 vs expected Rs 60,000) and WO25-02456 (Rs 18,824 vs expected Rs 20,700) were both below expected cost. The records do not show that the repeat work was needed, and no complaint is linked. Crew logs, photos and inspection records should be checked before any conclusion is drawn.
mitigations.based_on: ghost_bill_examples WO25-02475 cost_inr 45505 expected_inr 60000; WO25-02456 cost_inr 18824 expected_inr 20700; evidence: no complaint linked

upheld: Four jobs billed above benchmark, Rs 3.58L over expected: WO25-01942 (2.67x), WO25-00140 (2.40x), WO25-00382 (2.29x), WO25-01812 (1.71x).
Five bills totaling Rs 2.20L have no linked complaint. Four named bills repeat earlier same-contractor jobs on the same segment 1 to 4 days before: WO25-02487, WO25-02461, WO25-02475, WO25-02456.

28 jobs totaling Rs 6.63L were paid while under the Defect Liability Period, including WO25-00523, WO25-02424, WO25-01164 and WO25-00274. Site checks are needed to see whether each was a defect the contractor should have fixed free.
accepted_context: Pumping and desilting in flood-prone wards may need more labour and time, which may explain part of the gap on WO25-00382, WO25-01942 and WO25-00140. The records do not yet prove this.
WO25-02475 (Rs 45,505 vs Rs 60,000 expected) and WO25-02456 (Rs 18,824 vs Rs 20,700 expected) cost less than benchmark. The repeat may reflect fresh damage after rain.
Heavy rain fell in 120 of 287 jobs' weeks, so some new damage on recently resurfaced roads, such as WO25-01164, may be weather-related.
Reopen rate is 9.1% against 24.4% expected, and the median rate ratio is 1.015. Durability and overall billing are close to peers.
judge.ruling: The four overbilled jobs stand as charges to check. Their bills are well above benchmark, and the records do not yet explain the gap. Pumping and desilting may explain part of it, but this is not proven. The five no-complaint bills stand as checks. Four named bills repeat same-contractor jobs 1 to 4 days earlier with no complaint linked. Two cost less than benchmark, so fresh rain damage is possible. The 28 DLP-paid jobs need site checks to see whether the contractor should have fixed defects at no charge. Rain may explain some damage. This ruling makes no finding of fraud.
judge.action: Verify measured quantities, line-item bills and site photos for WO25-01942, WO25-00140, WO25-00382 and WO25-01812, and recover any excess above benchmark that the checks cannot justify.
